awarding_body.detail: The MOE's own Major Policies page presents the INTENSE Program as the Ministry's own initiative, and the participating universities describe the same programme as MOE-led with the National Development Council funding scholarships and partner companies providing stipends and internships. This matches the record's awarding body (MOE with the NDC, participating universities and partner companies) exactly.
awarding_body.quote: The Ministry of Education (MOE) has launched the "International Industrial Talents Education Special Program (INTENSE Program)" for talents coming to Taiwan for study and employment after graduation. (MOE) | "The INTENSE Program is an industry-academia collaboration initiative launched by Taiwan's Ministry of Education." (NTUT OIA) | "This program is approved by the Ministry of Education (MOE), Taiwan." (KMU)

deadline.detail: The MOE policy page states no application deadline at all, and every participating university publishes its own window - exactly as the record says. All four windows cited in the record were verified against the universities' own pages: NCHU 2027 Spring 10 Sep - 12 Oct 2026 (GMT+8; the Semiconductor programme has a second window 6 - 30 Oct 2026); NCU 2027 Spring 1 - 22 Oct 2026; KMU 2027 Spring 21 Sep - 23 Oct 2026 (Taiwan time); NTUT 2027 Fall student nomination deadline 10 Mar 2027. On the check date (12 Oct 2026) the NCHU window closes today and the NCU and KMU windows remain open, so currently-open cycles are confirmed. (NCKU also ran a Spring 2027 INTENSE window, 23 Sep - 13 Oct 2026, per its application portal.)
deadline.quote: "Application: Sep. 10, 2026, 10:00 AM - Oct. 12, 2026, 5:00 PM (GMT+8)" (NCHU) | "the application period running from October 1 to October 22, 2026" (NCU) | "Application Period: September 21, 2026 9:00 ~ October 23, 2026 17:00" (KMU) | "Student nomination deadline: March 10, 2027" (NTUT)

eligibility.detail: Confirmed: applicants must meet the MOE Regulations Regarding International Students Undertaking Studies in Taiwan (NCHU: "Must meet the MOE Regulations Regarding International Students Undertaking Studies in Taiwan"); English-taught programmes require CEFR B1 at admission (NCHU: "CEFR B1+"; NCU programmes are English-taught); nationality targets differ by programme with Vietnam, Indonesia, the Philippines and Thailand commonly named (NCU's Advanced Mechanical Engineering Program is "open to applicants from Vietnam, Indonesia, Philippines, and Thailand"). CONTRADICTED: the record's claim that Chinese-taught programmes require TOCFL Level B1 - NCHU's own table puts TOCFL A2 as the application requirement with B1 only needed to continue the scholarship ("Chinese-taught | TOCFL A2+ | TOCFL B1 by the 3rd semester"), and NCHU's FAQ states "those applying for Chinese-taught programs must hold at least TOCFL A2". UNCONFIRMED: the sub-claim that some programmes are open to students of all nationalities - no page I read states this; named nationalities are programme-specific.
eligibility.quote: Chinese-taught | TOCFL A2+ | TOCFL B1 by the 3rd semester (NCHU language table; columns: Program Language | Application Requirement | Continued Scholarship Requirement) | "Applicants for English-taught programs must have at least CEFR B1 level, while those applying for Chinese-taught programs must hold at least TOCFL A2." (NCHU FAQ) | "Must meet the MOE Regulations Regarding International Students Undertaking Studies in Taiwan." (NCHU) | "the Advanced Mechanical Engineering Program (open to applicants from Vietnam, Indonesia, Philippines, and Thailand)" (NCU)

funding.detail: The award is genuinely fully funded, not tuition-only. MOE: the government covers tuition and other administrative costs for up to two years and participating companies provide a living allowance of at least NTD 10,000 per month plus an internship allowance at or above minimum wage. University pages confirm and itemise: NCHU NT$50,000 tuition per semester up to 2 years, NT$10,000+ monthly stipend, airfare subsidy (NT$9,000 New Southbound / NT$35,000 Europe-America) and arrival administrative support (NT$10,000 / NT$25,000); NCU full tuition and credit waivers up to 2 years, one-way airfare, initial administrative expense support and NT$10,000 monthly stipend; KMU NT$10,000 monthly living allowance plus tuition and miscellaneous fees, initial administrative expenses and one-time airfare. Continued funding in year 2 requires passing TOCFL and satisfactory university/enterprise evaluation.
funding.quote: "The Taiwanese government covers tuition fees and other administrative costs for up to two years. Participating companies provide each student with a living allowance at least NTD10,000 per month and an internship allowance (above or equal minimum wage)." (MOE) | "Recipients will receive a monthly living allowance of NT$10,000. In addition, tuition and miscellaneous fees, initial administrative expenses upon first arrival in Taiwan, and one-time airfare will also be covered." (KMU) | "full tuition and credit waivers for up to two years, a one-way flight ticket to Taiwan, initial administrative expense support, and a monthly stipend of NT$10,000 sponsored by industry partners" (NCU)

degree_levels.detail: Master's-level INTENSE programmes were read at NCHU (International Master Program in Smart Manufacturing; INTENSE Overseas Master's Program in Semiconductor), KMU (International Master's Program for Talent Cultivation in Electronic Materials), NTUT (Master's programmes for 2027 Fall) and NCU (graduate tracks), and Taiwan Tech publishes INTENSE guidelines for an Undergraduate (Bachelor) programme as well as graduate programmes. The record's "Master's, Bachelor's" is correct as the levels offered. Note: the Taiwan-Vietnam INTACT base description also mentions doctoral-level offerings for some partner tracks, which the record does not list; this is additive, not a contradiction of the two levels given.

(KMU) | "Department of Mechanical Engineering Master's Degree - English" (NCHU) | "Undergraduate program (Bachelor)" ... "2027 Spring Semester (Feb. entry) Application Period: Jul. 1 to sept. 11 (end at 12:00 noon), 2026" (NTUST INTENSE guidelines)

recommended_field_updates.deadline_text: No single INTENSE deadline - each participating university sets its own application window per intake. Verified windows: NCHU 2027 Spring, Sep. 10, 2026, 10:00 AM - Oct. 12, 2026, 5:00 PM (GMT+8) (Semiconductor programme: Oct. 6 - Oct. 30, 2026); NCU 2027 Spring, October 1 to October 22, 2026; KMU 2027 Spring, September 21, 2026 9:00 - October 23, 2026 17:00 (Taiwan time); NCU sister windows e.g. NCKU Spring 2027 Sep 23 - Oct 13, 2026; NTUT (Taipei Tech) 2027 Fall student nomination deadline: March 10, 2027.
recommended_field_updates.verification_notes: Programme verified live on 2026-10-12 against the MOE policy page and five partner-university pages. Deadline claim is exactly right and per-university; it changes every cycle, so re-check each university's own INTENSE/admissions page rather than any central page (the MOE page publishes no deadline). Known cycle for 2027 Spring: NCHU window closed 2026-10-12; NCU closed 2026-10-22; KMU closed 2026-10-23; next anchor date is NTUT's 2027 Fall nomination deadline of 2027-03-10. One eligibility claim needs correcting: Chinese-taught admission requirement is TOCFL A2 (not B1); TOCFL B1 is only required by the 3rd semester/second year to continue the scholarship. Recorded official_source_url (gocfs.ntu.edu.tw) is NTU's overseas-compatriot advising division homepage and carries no INTENSE content; it was replaced with the MOE programme page. Windows shift each intake (e.g. NCHU's 2027 Spring window differs from its general international-student window of Aug 15 - Sep 30, 2026).

notes_for_reviewer: Verdict is 'conflicting' solely because of one eligibility sub-claim: the record says Chinese-taught programmes require TOCFL Level B1, but every official page read (NCHU programme page and FAQ; NCKU's language requirements) puts TOCFL A2 as the admission requirement, with B1 needed only by the 3rd semester to continue the scholarship. Everything else - awarding body, all four deadline windows, full funding, and Master's/Bachelor's levels - verified exactly as recorded. A human should decide whether to correct the eligibility wording to 'Chinese-taught: TOCFL A2 at admission, TOCFL B1 by the 3rd semester for continued scholarship' and whether to keep the record's 'Master's, Bachelor's' levels or add Doctoral (some INTACT base tracks describe doctoral offerings). The sub-claim 'some programmes open to students of all nationalities' could not be confirmed from any page read; nationality targets are set per programme.
